name: Zero
why: 1: the number 0 has the single digit 0.

name: Up to 100
why: 91: 0 to 9 (10), then 10 to 99 without 11, 22, …, 99 (81). 100 has two zeros side by side.

name: Leading zeros are not digits
why: 819. Written as 0007, the number 7 would seem to repeat its zeros. Zeros in front of a number are not digits of it.

name: Counting from a
why: Count up to b, minus the count up to a − 1. Taking away the count up to a loses 123 itself.

name: Up to 10¹⁸
why: Counting one by one is impossible. The answer is 1 (for 0) plus 9 + 9² + … + 9¹⁸: a k-digit number has 9 choices for each place.

name: A big range
why: A digit DP works on the 18 places of each end.

name: A tight path that breaks early
From ten nines to 10¹¹
why: 9¹¹ = 31,381,059,609: both ends repeat a digit, and every number between has 11 digits.

name: Many ranges
why: Small ranges at the edges: single numbers, a range that crosses 100, and a range that starts at a power of 10.
